about: Tourism-as-an-industry figures for the Algarve and Portugal from official statistics (INE monthly tourist accommodation, INE airport survey for Faro, Turismo de Portugal RNAL open data). Latest accommodation and airport period: September 2026. Every number is as published by the source; none is rounded by us. Provisional (Po) and preliminary (Pe) flags follow the INE metadata note. Algarve = NUTS II Algarve (code 150 in NUTS 2024 for nights and guests, code 15 in the revenue indicator).

registered_local_accommodation.title: Registered Alojamento Local establishments (RNAL), Faro district (= Algarve), by municipality
registered_local_accommodation.unit: Number of registered establishments; beds = sum of NrUtentes (maximum guests registered)

source.publisher: Turismo de Portugal I.P., Registo Nacional de Alojamento Local, layer "Estabelecimentos de Alojamento Local"
source.licence: CC BY 4.0 (as listed on dados.gov.pt: cc-by)

registered_local_accommodation.note: Counts are registrations in the register at the query date, not guaranteed active listings or occupied units. Totals added by us from the 16 municipality counts; Faro district total 44,890 matches the sum. The layer shown covers mainland districts only (sum of the 18 mainland districts is 112,122); islands not checked.

headlines.text: In September 2026 Portuguese tourist accommodation recorded 3.4 million guests and 8.7 million overnight stays, up 2.5% and 2.0% on September 2025; total revenue was EUR 890.2 million, up 6.1%.

The Algarve took 27.5% of all overnight stays in the country in September 2026, the biggest regional share, ahead of Greater Lisbon (22.2%) and the North (18.8%). INE puts Algarve nights at 2,388.0 thousand, up 0.6%, with resident nights down 2.0% and non-resident nights up 1.4%.

Guests in the Algarve stayed longest on mainland Portugal in September 2026, 3.92 nights on average (only Madeira, at 4.55, was longer); the Algarve also had the second-highest average room rate, EUR 155.6, behind Greater Lisbon at EUR 182.2.
The Algarve earned 27.0% of national accommodation revenue in September 2026 (26.3% of room revenue), second to Greater Lisbon at 28.0%.

Albufeira was the second-busiest municipality in the country in September 2026 with 893.2 thousand overnight stays (10.3% of the national total, +2.2%); the British were the largest source market nationally with 19.1% of non-resident nights.

gaps.what: Faro airport traffic from ANA directly
gaps.why: Not requested: INE airports survey (ANA/ANAC/INE) gave the monthly Faro series, so ANA pages were not read. No bot check was met.

gaps.what: Algarve RevPAR and ADR by month as a series
gaps.why: INE publishes regional RevPAR/ADR only inside the press-release charts (images) for the latest month; no monthly regional indicator code was found. Only the text figure ADR EUR 155.6 (Sept 2026) is recorded, as a headline.

gaps.what: Algarve guest and revenue series flag per value
gaps.why: INE API returns no per-value flag; flags taken from the indicator metadata note (Jan-Aug 2026 provisional, Sep 2026 preliminary).

gaps.what: Whole-economy tourism figures (GDP share, employment, Tourism Satellite Account)
gaps.why: Not retrieved in this task; news search suggested INE published a 2025 figure but it was not read from the source.

gaps.what: TravelBI terms of use and open-data terms
gaps.why: Home page read (HTTP 200) but its terms are not in the static HTML (page appears script-rendered). The home page lists themes (Alojamento, Movimentos Aereos, Tendencias, Turismo Internacional and others), market pages, SIGTUR and Dados Abertos, with an optional sign-in. No TravelBI data was used; its figures largely repeat INE. Terms unread, so reuse not cleared.
The licence text for INE data was not re-read; the licence field says attribution to INE and asks for confirmation before publication. dados.gov.pt lists INE tourism datasets as cc-by.
The ArcGIS layer returned mainland districts only; Azores and Madeira not checked (not needed for the Algarve).
INE connections were reset several times by the egress proxy; each call was retried after a pause and finally succeeded. No refusal (403 or bot check) was met anywhere.
